subject: Hosted API p95 regression — investigation points to client-side retries/backoff
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@cartology.io>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cartology.io
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 latency and 503s this morning

Hi Rohan —

We started seeing a sharp jump in p95/p99 and intermittent 5xxs from Redwood hosted API around 07:50 PDT this morning. Our dashboard (attached screenshot) shows client-facing errors and latency spikes that coincided with a private sale event — this is causing checkout failures.

We rely on the hosted endpoints for sync scoring; this is high-impact for the business. Can you confirm if there was a platform incident or maintenance window? Happy to share logs or sample request IDs.

Attachments: p95-spike-overview-20270514.png

Thanks,
Alice

Engineering Lead — Cartology
alice.chen@cartology.io

Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency and 503s this morning

Alice — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot.

Marissa (AE) and Sergio (on-call infra) are looped in. Sergio: can you triage ingress and model-serving p95/p99 for Cartology's tenant + any upstream errors? Alice, if you can also attach a couple of request IDs and the SDK version your service is using, that'll help.

We’ll get back with an initial read within 90 minutes.

—Rohan

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@cartology.io>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:10:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency and 503s this morning

Quick triage update:
- Platform infra: no scheduled maintenance. Core model-serving nodes (GPU pools) report stable tail compute latency for the times Alice called out.
- Ingress: we observed a ~3.8x jump in incoming request QPS to Cartology’s tenant at 07:51, lasting ~18 minutes. Ingress 5xxs spiked after the QPS jump.
- Error surface: most 5xxs map to our rate limiter returning 429/503 when the burst exceeded the tenant’s reserved throughput; compute layer did not show proportional tail latency.

Prelim hypothesis: an amplification effect — a large number of short client-side timeouts + aggressive SDK retry/backoff caused fan-out, inflating apparent p95/p99 and pushing the tenant into rate limiting. I’m attaching a heatmap of request retries across clients for the time window.

Attachments: ingress-retries-heatmap.csv

Next steps:
1) Alice — please confirm SDK version and sample timeout/retry config.
2) We’ll correlate request ids and provide a timeline of retry bursts.
3) If client retries are aggressive, recommend increasing client request timeout and enabling exponential backoff on retries immediately.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior SRE — Serving
Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@cartology.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:25:32 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency and 503s this morning

Thanks Sergio — details below.

We run a serverless checkout worker that calls Redwood via the official JS SDK v1.2.3. Our HTTP client is configured for low tail latency: connect+read timeout set to 800ms, with maxRetries=4 and a fixed retry interval of 200ms (we implemented that to try to keep checkout latency low).

Sample snippet (attached):
- timeoutMs: 800
- retries: 4
- retryDelayMs: 200

We did observe a large number of consecutive calls from a small set of IPs (our worker fleet) at 07:50 — the fleet was under load due to the sale. We are happy to change config if that reduces impact.

Attachment: sdk-http-config-snippet.txt

Alice

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@cartology.io>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 13:00:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency and 503s this morning

Thanks Alice — that confirms the hypothesis. More detailed analysis attached. Key findings:
- Compute layer p95/p99 for Cartology’s model shards remained within historical baselines (no per-token slowness).
- The ingress pipeline saw a spike in concurrent in-flight requests due to retries; many of those were retries from requests that had in-flight upstreams completing successfully but the client had already timed out and retried. 
- Net effect: artificial QPS amplification (observed fan-out factor up to 5x for some request patterns) causing burst quota exhaustion and rate-limited 429/503s.

Immediate remediation (recommended):
1) Cartology to increase SDK client timeout to >= 3000ms and switch to exponential backoff (start 250ms, multiplier 2) with jitter; reduce maxRetries to 2 for checkout path.
2) On Redwood side, we’ll add a short-lived token-level smoothing window (10s rolling) to avoid sharp quota eviction from bursty retries and publish guidance for clients about sensible retry policies.
3) We’ll also surface per-request retry headers so we can attribute retry amplification in future incidents.

I’ll follow up with a timeline export and a recommended config change snippet. We can also coordinate a short maintenance-free test window to validate.

Attachments: ingress-retries-heatmap.csv (detailed), p95-spike-overview-20270514.png (overlay)

—Sergio

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@cartology.io>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API p95 regression — investigation points to client-side retries/backoff

Alice — thanks again for the quick info and for being responsive. To summarize for Execs and the account:
- Root cause: client-side timeout/retry configuration amplified request traffic during Cartology’s sale, producing a spike in ingress QPS and triggering tenant-level rate limiting (429/503). Our compute latency was within expectations.
- Immediate customer actions: increase client timeout to 3s, adopt exponential backoff with jitter, reduce max retries on checkout flows. Sergio’s team will provide the config snippet and a replay window to test.
- Redwood actions: publish retry guidance, enable a 10s smoothing window to damp retry-induced bursts, add retry-attribution headers, and offer observability dashboards for retries.

Commercial: given the customer impact — we propose a one-week credit against hosted consumption for the affected window while we roll mitigations. Alice, please confirm you’re OK with the remediation plan and the credit; we’ll also set up a 30-minute sync to validate after changes.

We’ll follow-up with a post-incident write-up once actions are complete.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
